# Helper functions

These are defined once and used by all the examples below.

```{r helpers}
my_mean <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sum(x) / length(x)
}

my_var <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sum((x - my_mean(x))^2) / (length(x) - 1)
}

my_sd <- function(x) sqrt(my_var(x))

my_median <- function(x) {
  x <- sort(x[!is.na(x)])
  n <- length(x)
  if (n %% 2 == 1) x[(n + 1) / 2] else mean(x[n / 2 + 0:1])
}

my_summary <- function(x) {
  c(n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean = my_mean(x),
    median = my_median(x),
    sd = my_sd(x),
    min = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}

my_t_test <- function(x, y) {
  nx <- length(x); ny <- length(y)
  vx <- my_var(x); vy <- my_var(y)

  se <- sqrt(vx / nx + vy / ny)
  t  <- (my_mean(x) - my_mean(y)) / se
  df <- (vx / nx + vy / ny)^2 /
        ((vx / nx)^2 / (nx - 1) + (vy / ny)^2 / (ny - 1))
  p  <- 2 * pt(-abs(t), df)

  list(t = t, df = df, p.value = p)
}
```

# 1. `lapply`: returns a list

`lapply()` applies a function to each element of a list or vector and always returns a **list**.

```{r lapply}
nums <- list(a = c(1, 2, 3, 4), b = c(10, 20, 30), c = c(5, NA, 15))

lapply(nums, my_mean)
lapply(nums, my_summary)

# A data frame is a list of columns
lapply(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")], my_sd)
```

# 2. `sapply`: simplifies to a vector or matrix

`sapply()` works like `lapply()` but simplifies the result to a vector or matrix when possible.

```{r sapply}
sapply(nums, my_mean)                                 # named numeric vector
sapply(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")], my_summary)    # matrix: stats x variables

# Anonymous function: range of each column
sapply(mtcars[, 1:4], function(col) max(col) - min(col))
```

# 3. `tapply`: apply by group

`tapply()` applies a function to a vector, split by one or more grouping factors.

```{r tapply}
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$cyl, my_mean)   # mean mpg by number of cylinders
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$am, my_sd)      # sd of mpg by transmission

# Two grouping factors give a matrix
tapply(mtcars$mpg, list(cyl = mtcars$cyl, am = mtcars$am), my_mean)

# Returning more than one value per group gives a list
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$cyl, my_summary)
```

# 4. `apply`: rows or columns of a matrix

`apply()` applies a function over the rows (`1`) or columns (`2`) of a matrix. Use numeric columns only, since a data frame is converted to a matrix.

```{r apply}
m <- as.matrix(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")])

apply(m, 2, my_mean)           # column means
apply(m, 1, sum)[1:5]          # row sums (first 5 cars)
apply(m, 2, my_summary)        # summary of each column

# Extra arguments are passed through
apply(m, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.25, 0.75))
```

# 5. `mapply`: several inputs in parallel

`mapply()` applies a function to several vectors or lists in parallel, element by element.

```{r mapply}
mapply(function(x, y) x + y, 1:5, 6:10)

# Repeat each value a different number of times
mapply(rep, times = 1:4, x = 4:1)

# Welch t statistic for several variables, split by transmission (am)
vars <- c("mpg", "hp", "wt")
tstats <- mapply(function(v) {
  auto   <- mtcars[[v]][mtcars$am == 0]
  manual <- mtcars[[v]][mtcars$am == 1]
  my_t_test(auto, manual)$t
}, vars)
tstats

# Two varying inputs: mean of each column with a different trim proportion
mapply(function(col, trim) mean(mtcars[[col]], trim = trim),
       col  = c("mpg", "hp", "wt"),
       trim = c(0, 0.1, 0.2))
```
